title: Regular Expression Matching
keyIdea: dp[i][j] = s[i..] matches p[j..]. If p[j + 1] is '*': skip 'p[j]*' (dp[i][j + 2]) or, if s[i] matches p[j], use it once and stay (dp[i + 1][j]). Otherwise s[i] must match p[j] ('.' matches any) and dp[i + 1][j + 1]. Fill from the end.

approaches.name: Bottom-up DP on suffixes
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). dp[m][n] = true; for i = m..0, j = n − 1..0: first = s[i] matches p[j]; star → dp[i][j + 2] || (first && dp[i + 1][j]); else first && dp[i + 1][j + 1].

quiz.q: When standing on p[j], why check p[j + 1] == '*'?
options: A following '*' changes p[j] into 'zero or more', so the choice is made here
Skip it entirely (j + 2), or use it for one matching letter and stay on j (i + 1)

quiz.q: Why does row i = m (empty s) matter?
options: Patterns like a*b* can still match the empty string
